contract.label: Required, 1–150 Unicode code points. Optional visible bold label carries no heading semantics; hidden labels are not accessible names.
contract.grid: 1–5 rows, 1–3 items per row; weights narrow=1, standard=2, wide=3; alignment start/center/end, omission fills the cell; grid lines none/rows/outer.
contract.nesting: Direct layout children and markdown are forbidden. A layout/container path may contain at most two composite levels.
contract.wide_content: At most one carousel, data table or chart per row; a chart must have strictly more than half the total row weight.
contract.fallback: Exactly the eight documented stable block types, rendered instead of the grid. Omission remains omitted on input; Slack normalizes it to an empty array.
contract.context: Every nested child and fallback block must be permitted on the enclosing surface; existing aggregate chart and text limits still apply.

library_policy.block_budget: Conservatively count one for each layout label/block and each nested block against the existing 50-message/100-view limits. Count containers on a layout-containing path, but preserve legacy container-only accounting. Check fallback as replacement content: use the greater primary/fallback cost, not their sum.
library_policy.budget_caveat: The documentation explicitly says nested content consumes the enclosing budget but gives no formula. The receiving message API accepted 50 layouts each containing a divider. The conservative library policy is not represented as a measured Slack rejection.
library_policy.character_budget: Retain existing field and message-wide markdown/data-table bounds. Do not invent a global character threshold or assign the label to unrelated text budgets.
library_policy.receiving_validation: Prefer documented contextual restrictions over permissive schema-only validation. Real chat.update rejected nested markdown, a direct nested layout, three composite levels, message alert and a half-width chart; a 3:2 chart row succeeded.

limitations: Initial message-schema probes incorrectly included text in a restricted validation envelope; their errors are retained and are not evidence of layout rejection. Corrected block-only probes follow.
An initial table probe omitted a required caption and is not a valid child-support comparison.
These are synthetic contract probes, not yet a claim of ten-language live acceptance or visual/browser interaction coverage.
No old Slack client was available to verify actual fallback rendering. Mobile wrapping and screen-reader behavior are documented behavior, not live-tested claims.
